findings.finding: This is the first hearing_number 2 record ever actually filed for M1-KESTREL. moot/hearing-3.json, hearing-4.json, and hearing-5.json each repeatedly cite a 'Hearing 2' as settled prior record (specific directions to correct AUTH-002/Fecitt and to log five named authorities), but Hearing 1's own record (moot/hearing-1.json) already found no such file existed, and a fresh directory check confirms hearing-2.json was absent until this hearing wrote it. This Tribunal does not treat hearing-3/4/5.json as binding prior record for anything decided below - Hearing 1 already said they should not be relied on until rerun against the documents that now actually exist, and that finding is adopted, not revisited. Where this hearing's own independent findings happen to converge with what those stale files predicted a 'Hearing 2' would find, that convergence is coincidental (both readings independently confronting the same actual record), not deference to an unfiled precedent.

The core doctrine for the lead heads is correctly stated and, on the verification tiers actually logged in authorities.json, adequately supported. Kuzel v Roche Products Ltd [2008] EWCA Civ 380 (AUTH-003) correctly states that the legal burden of showing the reason for dismissal never shifts to the claimant, and that the tribunal must consider the claimant's alleged reason once the employer's stated reason is rejected. Beatt v Croydon Health Services NHS Trust [2017] EWCA Civ 401 (AUTH-004) correctly states that whether a disclosure was protected is an objective question for the tribunal, not a function of the employer's belief. NHS Manchester v Fecitt [2011] EWCA Civ 1190 (AUTH-002) correctly states the 'materially influenced' causation threshold for s.47B, and - since Hearing 1 - its superseded co-worker/vicarious-liability limb has actually been corrected with a primary-source citation (ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E), inserted by ERRA 2013 s.19, verified live against legislation.gov.uk and cross-checked against the enacting provision). This is genuine doctrinal progress since Hearing 1, not a repeat of it: the correction three stale, unreliable hearing files claimed was repeatedly ordered and never made has, on this actual record, now been made, with a primary source behind it.

A live, unaddressed adverse-authority gap exists in the claimant's own theory, and it is a doctrinal gap, not the fact gap Hearing 1 already found. ERA 1996 s.43B(1), as amended by Enterprise and Regulatory Reform Act 2013 s.17 (reversing Parkins v Sodexho Ltd [2002] IRLR 109), requires a reasonable belief that the disclosure was made in the public interest; Chesterton Global Ltd v Nurmohamed [2017] EWCA Civ 979 sets the governing test (objectively reasonable belief; the disclosure need not be exclusively in the public interest provided a section of the public beyond the discloser is engaged). final/case_theory_memo.md Section 3 lists the public-interest element only as one item in the Further and Better Particulars still needed (a fact gap, F-010) - it never actually states or engages the governing legal test itself anywhere in the document. opposition/opposition_case.md Part B.1(i) does state the test correctly and applies it as a genuine, non-manufactured obstacle. A doctrinal hearing testing whether adverse authority has been addressed finds that, on the claimant's side, it has not: the claimant's theory has correctly flagged the missing fact but has not yet grappled with the legal test that fact will have to satisfy.

The six additional authorities the opposing case relies on - British Home Stores Ltd v Burchell [1978] IRLR 379, Iceland Frozen Foods Ltd v Jones [1982] IRLR 439/[1983] ICR 17, Polkey v A E Dayton Services Ltd [1988] AC 344, Chesterton Global Ltd v Nurmohamed [2017] EWCA Civ 979, J v DLA Piper UK LLP [2010] UKEAT/0263/09, and the Enterprise and Regulatory Reform Act 2013 s.17 amendment itself - are none of them logged in authorities.json (confirmed by direct inspection: the file runs only to AUTH-007, and none of these six appears anywhere in it) and none appears in research/research_log.md either. Each carries a citation, a stated verification tier, and named secondary sources within the prose of opposition_case.md itself, but docs/OPERATING_RULES.md is explicit that 'a citation that only appears in another AI-generated document is not verification.' opposition_case.md is exactly such a document - a case-theory narrative, not this matter's authority ledger - and its internal citation list is not a substitute for a schemas/authority.schema.json-conformant entry in authorities.json with its own verification_status and primary_source_link fields, the same standard already applied inside this matter's own record to AUTH-007 (Raison), which was correctly held back as a research lead rather than relied upon until logged. This is a fresh, freestanding finding: Hearing 1 never tested authority-ledger integrity (that was not its remit), so this is not a repeat of anything already decided, and it recurs on the opposition's side of the record specifically, as the same asymmetry the (non-binding) stale hearing-3/4/5 files independently guessed at.

This Tribunal's own tool contract (agents/judiciary/ROLE.md: Read, Grep, Glob only) cannot independently verify any of the six unlogged authorities against a primary source this session, the same limitation this Tribunal flagged in Hearing 1 for its own ET Rule 29/37 citations. From general legal recollection, not independently re-verified this session and flagged accordingly: Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods, Polkey, Chesterton v Nurmohamed, and J v DLA Piper are all real, well-known, correctly-attributed English employment authorities consistent with the propositions claimed for them, and nothing about them resembles the shape-plausible-but-fabricated pattern that correctly caught the seeded Whitfield authority. This Tribunal does not find them fabricated. It finds them unverified for this matter's own recordkeeping purposes, which is a narrower and more precise finding than 'unreliable,' and the two should not be conflated.

The Hearing 1 precondition on ISS-003/ISS-004 advancing at all - Further and Better Particulars of the disclosure(s)' content, recipient, form, and date (F-010), the public-interest belief basis, and their sequencing against the disciplinary process (F-012) - remains completely unmet. facts/facts.json still records F-010 and F-012 as UNKNOWN, unchanged since Hearing 1, and final/case_theory_memo.md's own Section 3 confirms this in its own terms ('what the lead theory needs and does not yet have'). This hearing tests doctrine, not proof - so it does not re-run Hearing 3's future evidentiary inquiry - but it cannot ignore that the doctrine it has just confirmed sound (Kuzel/Beatt/corrected-Fecitt) has nothing yet to operate on. Hearing 1 distinguished this gap from the disability/victimisation cluster's fatal defect on the basis that disclosure content is 'specific, discoverable factual detail a genuine claimant ordinarily already possesses and could supply immediately if put to it.' That premise is what justified a conditional pass rather than a strike. One full hearing cycle later, with no explanation offered anywhere in the record for the continued absence of that detail, the premise is not yet disproved, but it is no longer free-standing: this Tribunal notes plainly that if F-010/F-012 remain unstated going into Hearing 3, the 'genuinely discoverable, merely not yet supplied' characterisation becomes progressively harder to sustain, and the live question stops being whether particulars are outstanding and starts being why they still are.

ISS-002 (contingent on continuity, F-008 still UNKNOWN) raises no live doctrinal dispute at this hearing - Burchell and Iceland Frozen Foods are correctly identified in opposition_case.md Part B.2 as the governing fairness doctrine that will apply once a stated reason for dismissal (F-020) exists, and are correctly held in reserve rather than applied to facts that do not yet exist. No repair is required on ISS-002's doctrine specifically; its continuity gate remains the operative constraint, unchanged from Hearing 1.

ISS-009's remedy doctrine (Polkey deduction; TULRCA 1992 s.207A ACAS Code uplift) is correctly and candidly described by the opposing case (Part B.3) as genuinely two-edged rather than a one-sided Respondent advantage - that is an accurate statement of the law and is accepted. Polkey itself, however, is among the six authorities not yet logged in authorities.json (see above), so this doctrine cannot presently be treated as resting on a verified matter authority, only on a correct but unlogged legal proposition.

ISS-005 to ISS-008 (disability cluster, victimisation), struck at Hearing 1 for a pleading defect, are not revisited. Neither final/case_theory_memo.md nor opposition/opposition_case.md attempts to revive them with new content, correctly treating Hearing 1's strike as settled. J v DLA Piper UK LLP, while a genuine and correctly-described authority on the qualifying-impairment/stress-reaction distinction, bears on a claim that does not currently exist and is noted for the future record only, not applied to anything live today.

ISS-001 (limitation) is not decided at this hearing and no doctrinal development changes its posture. The EDT (F-002) and ACAS Day A (F-004) remain assumed/unknown exactly as at Hearing 1. This Tribunal notes, without deciding anything on it, that research/research_log.md records a further complication for whoever eventually litigates the actual dates: multiple secondary sources (not independently verified against legislation.gov.uk this session) suggest the Employment Rights Act 2025 may extend the primary limitation period to six months, which would matter to the s.111(2)(b)/s.207B calculation once real dates exist - flagged as a research lead for Hearing 3 or whichever later stage actually fixes the dates, not resolved here.

repairs_required: Log British Home Stores Ltd v Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods Ltd v Jones, Polkey v A E Dayton Services Ltd, Chesterton Global Ltd v Nurmohamed, J v DLA Piper UK LLP, and the ERRA 2013 s.17 amendment in authorities.json with schemas/authority.schema.json-conformant entries (verification_status, primary_source_link, treatment) before any of them is treated as part of this matter's verified authority record - a narrative citation inside opposition_case.md is not a substitute for the ledger, per docs/OPERATING_RULES.md's own rule that a citation appearing only in another AI-generated document is not verification.

The claimant's case theory must engage doctrinally with ERA 1996 s.43B(1) as amended by ERRA 2013 s.17 and the Chesterton Global v Nurmohamed reasonable-belief/public-interest test specifically - not merely flag the underlying fact gap (F-010) - before Hearing 3. As currently drafted, final/case_theory_memo.md states the lead doctrine (Kuzel/Beatt/Fecitt) but does not confront the one adverse legal test squarely raised against it.

Produce the Further and Better Particulars of the disclosure(s) - content, recipient, form, date, public-interest belief basis, and sequencing against the disciplinary process (F-010, F-012) - directed at Hearing 1 and still completely unmet. This repair is repeated, not because it was overlooked, but because nothing has changed since Hearing 1: if it remains unmet going into Hearing 3, the 'genuinely discoverable, merely outstanding' characterisation that justified a conditional pass rather than a strike becomes harder to sustain, and Hearing 3 should treat continued, unexplained non-production as approaching the point a real tribunal's unless-order power exists to address, not as an ordinary thin-evidence question.

Obtain the actual EDT and the actual ACAS EC certificate (Day A and Day B) - directed at Hearing 1, still not done; unchanged and not re-litigated further here beyond confirming its continued absence.
Plead or evidence continuity of employment for ISS-002 (F-008) - directed at Hearing 1, still not done.
Confirm and correctly name the Respondent (F-025) - directed at Hearing 1, still not done.

Whoever runs Hearing 3 next must read this record (the first genuine hearing-2.json this matter has ever had) and should not treat the previously filed hearing-3.json, hearing-4.json, or hearing-5.json as settled prior record - Hearing 1 already found, and this hearing confirms, that those files rest on a 'Hearing 2' and case-theory documents that did not exist in the form those files described. They should be rerun against this actual record and the real final/case_theory_memo.md / opposition/opposition_case.md, not merely left in place because their outcome happens to resemble what an independent reading of the real record also finds.
disposition: Hearing 2 (DOCTRINAL_AND_AUTHORITY_CHALLENGE), M1-KESTREL, England & Wales Employment Tribunal, continuing this Tribunal's case-management function from Hearing 1 on the real record now actually before it. No head is struck or newly cleared at this hearing. ISS-003 (s.103A) and ISS-004 (s.47B) remain in the same conditional posture Hearing 1 left them in - proceeding, but not unconditionally - because the doctrine underlying them (Kuzel, Beatt, and Fecitt as now properly corrected for the ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E)/ERRA 2013 point) is sound and adequately verified at the tier this matter's own record uses throughout, and no adverse authority has emerged that defeats the heads outright. But this hearing adds two things Hearing 1 could not have tested and finds neither presently satisfied: first, the claimant's theory has not yet engaged the one squarely adverse legal test raised against it - the ERA 1996 s.43B(1)/ERRA 2013 s.17 public-interest reasonable-belief requirement as explained in Chesterton Global v Nurmohamed - only the underlying fact gap; second, six authorities the opposing case relies on (Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods, Polkey, Chesterton, J v DLA Piper, and the ERRA 2013 s.17 amendment) exist only as narrative citations in opposition_case.md and are not logged in this matter's own authority ledger, and cannot be treated as verified matter authorities until they are. Separately, and because it bears directly on how much longer the conditional-pass premise can hold, this hearing records that the Further and Better Particulars Hearing 1 required have still not been produced, with no explanation offered, one full hearing cycle later. ISS-002 remains contingent on continuity (unchanged), ISS-009 remains a parasitic remedy issue with sound but unlogged doctrine, ISS-005 to ISS-008 remain struck and are not revisited, and ISS-001 remains undecided. This matter proceeds to Hearing 3 in a materially tightened conditional posture, not the same posture it entered this hearing in.
reasons: This hearing's task is doctrine and authority, not proof - whether the legal test is correctly stated, whether the binding authorities actually say what is claimed for them, and what adverse authority has not been addressed. Testing the surviving heads against that standard confirms the core doctrine is sound: Kuzel's non-shifting legal burden, Beatt's objective assessment of protection, and Fecitt's 'materially influenced' causation threshold, now correctly qualified for the ERA 1996 s.47B(1A)-(1E) co-worker point with a primary source behind it for the first time in this matter's actual record, are all accurately stated and adequately verified at the tier (VERIFIED_SECONDARY_SOURCE, with one VERIFIED_PRIMARY_SOURCE qualification) this matter has consistently used. That is genuine progress since Hearing 1 and I have said so plainly rather than treating it as background. But applying the same standard evenhandedly means not stopping there. The claimant's theory names the public-interest element as a missing fact and stops; it does not test whether the doctrine governing that fact (ERRA 2013 s.17, Chesterton) has actually been engaged, which is precisely this hearing's remit rather than Hearing 1's or Hearing 3's - a doctrinal hearing exists to ask not only 'is the authority the claimant relies on sound' but 'has the claimant addressed the authority working against it,' and on this record it has not. Separately, and independently, I have applied this matter's own verification hierarchy to the opposing case's own new authorities rather than accepting them because they are correctly described and I recognise them as genuine from general legal knowledge - recognition is not the standard docs/OPERATING_RULES.md sets, logging in authorities.json with a documented trail is, and none of the six has been logged. I have been careful to distinguish 'unverified in this matter's own record' from 'doubted as authority' - I do not find these six fabricated, unlike the seeded Whitfield citation both sides independently and correctly rejected again this round, and conflating the two would misstate what I actually found. On the still-unmet Further and Better Particulars condition, I have not re-decided the evidentiary question - that remains Hearing 3's job, not mine, and it would be exactly the 'five identical arguments' failure this workflow exists to prevent for me to re-run Hearing 1's finding wholesale. What is properly mine to say is narrower and different: Hearing 1's distinction between the whistleblowing heads (curable, so conditional) and the disability/victimisation cluster (nothing left to amend, so struck) rested on an assumption that the missing content was genuinely close at hand. A full hearing cycle passing with no change and no explanation is itself a doctrinal-stage-relevant fact about how much longer that assumption can be relied on without becoming a fiction, and I have said so without purporting to decide the underlying evidentiary question myself. I have declined to treat the stale hearing-3/4/5.json files as prior authority for anything, consistent with Hearing 1's own finding, even where my own independent reading happens to land on similar ground (the AUTH-002 correction, the unlogged-authorities point) - that convergence is the record speaking for itself twice, not one unreliable file validating another.
concessions_made: Accepted that Kuzel, Beatt, and Fecitt (as now corrected) are accurately stated by both sides and adequately verified at this matter's own consistent tier; this hearing does not disturb any of that doctrine.

Accepted that the seeded fabricated authority (Whitfield v Anglia NHS Foundation Trust) was independently re-checked and correctly rejected again by both sides this round, on separate research passes reaching the same result, and needs no further attention at this hearing.

Accepted that the opposing case's own account of the six new authorities is candid about their verification tier and honestly two-edged where the law actually is (Part B.3 on Polkey/uplift; Part B.4 on Gallop cutting against the Respondent) - the deficiency found here is that they are unlogged, not that they were advanced in bad faith or overstated.
Accepted that neither side attempted to revive ISS-005 to ISS-008, correctly treating Hearing 1's strike as settled.

hot_bench_questions.question: If, once produced, the disclosure turns out to concern only the claimant's own contract or treatment with no wider public-interest element, does ISS-003/ISS-004 survive Chesterton Global v Nurmohamed at all - and where in the claimant's theory is that question actually engaged, rather than the underlying fact merely flagged as missing?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: Not answered anywhere in final/case_theory_memo.md. Section 3 lists the public-interest element among the particulars still needed but never states or applies the governing legal test (ERA 1996 s.43B(1) as amended, Chesterton) to test the theory against it. This Tribunal answers only that the gap exists and must be closed before Hearing 3, not what the answer would be.

hot_bench_questions.question: Why should this Tribunal treat Burchell, Iceland Frozen Foods, Polkey, Chesterton, and J v DLA Piper as part of this matter's verified record when none of them appears in authorities.json?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: It should not. opposition_case.md's own internal citation list, however candid about its sourcing tier, is not this matter's authority ledger, and docs/OPERATING_RULES.md says a citation appearing only in another AI-generated document is not verification. They remain unlogged, and are treated as such.

hot_bench_questions.question: One full hearing cycle after Hearing 1 required Further and Better Particulars of the disclosure as a precondition to these heads proceeding at all, why does F-010 still say UNKNOWN with no explanation given anywhere in the record?
hot_bench_questions.answer_summary: Not answered. Neither final/case_theory_memo.md nor opposition/opposition_case.md offers any account of why the particulars remain unproduced; the claimant's own memo restates the gap rather than closing or explaining it.

residual_uncertainty: This hearing tests doctrine and authority-record integrity, not proof - it does not and cannot say whether the disclosure, once particularised, will in fact satisfy the public-interest test, nor whether the six unlogged authorities would survive formal logging (this Tribunal has no basis, on its own Read/Grep/Glob tool contract, to say they would not - only that they have not yet been logged). Real disclosure of the actual communication could resolve the public-interest question in either direction. The tightened conditional posture recorded here reflects the doctrinal record as it now stands, not a prediction of how Hearing 3's evidentiary inquiry will come out. ISS-001 remains exactly as undecided as Hearing 1 left it and this hearing adds nothing to it beyond noting the Employment Rights Act 2025 extension question as an unresolved research lead for whenever real dates exist.
